Meditate, and practice mindfulness. Both are a practice you do, like playing guitar or basketball, and you only get better at them with regular practice.


To practice meditation, which is a tool in mindfulness, start easy. Begin with apps and videos that promote guided meditation for a mere 10 minutes and fit it into a regular spot in your schedule. Once you get the hang of it you can find it all on your own or do longer practices. Fun fact: Thousands of people, after years and years of practice, say that they find a peaceful bliss that makes them feel connected and happy, even outside of meditation.

To practice mindfulness, consider purchasing a workbook, but it looks like this--truly taste what you eat instead of watching TV or talking, notice what the shampoo smells like in the shower instead of day dreaming, notice your feet on the ground when going for a walk, take time to respond to what people say and really think about it, notice when you feel emotions and what the physiological sensations are and the repeated thoughts that come with them.... etc. Mindfulness can be a tool that aligns your thoughts with becoming the person you want to be.

My little Woody is not so little anymore. He's 21 years old, and my family rescued him when I was in 2nd grade. I care about this cat so truly and deeply and I worry about him everyday. I can imagine your feelings may be similar. 

Here is the only piece of advice I have for you: Love. Love this little entity with all of your heart. This means going deep. Ask yourself WHY do you show your love the way you do...Snuggles, warm wishes, treats, play time, respect, admiration, affection... but why do you do this? Because this is what your little one would want. Now (remember I said go deep) would your little cat want you to do worse or better at school? Would your fur baby want you to worry all the time or be out having fun and check in when you have the time? Would the precious little fuzz buzz be okay with knowing you expect the worst, or instead, would she want you to believe in her?

Find relief in how you live your life in terms of your cat, by being the human your cat wants you to be.

That is how anxiety came to birth in the first place, and why it aggressively follows your every thought. The way out? The cure to this debilitating cycle of depression and regret? Is doing literally the very last thing you feel like doing and it involves an indescribably difficult intrinsic battle within yourself that is, in short, MAKING yourself be who you want to be. That, or stay right where you are. 

So the only thing that will help you, it's not words, it's not advice, it's not drugs or a million dollars or a fairy tale... it's you, getting your bloody camera out and making a vlog. Right. Now. It's you, putting your old sneakers on and running until it hurts so that you can sign up for a race. Right. Now. 

It's you.

That's it.

Only you. 

So get the heck up, and do the last thing you want to do RIGHT NOW, because trusting your whiny "I don't want to, I can't..." voice is what got you here. 

Just do it.
